subject: EdgeWave - Optimize Toolkit: credit structure & technical tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@edgewave.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgewave.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluate Optimize toolkit for inference cost reduction

Markus —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. The tech team at EdgeWave was impressed by the batching and KV-cache features, but procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how credits vs. reserved commit interact with quantization recommendations. Two concrete asks: 1) can we see an example credit drawdown for our 3-month pilot (50M tokens/month) if we enable 4-bit quantization and prefix caching? 2) are there any SLA or support differences if we use a credits model vs a small reserved bucket?

Also copying Tom from procurement so he can start the paperwork if we get a suitable commercial outline.

—Sara
Head of ML, EdgeWave

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluate Optimize toolkit for inference cost reduction

Sara — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answers up front: we can produce a token-level sketch for the pilot and the SLA/support are identical for credits and reserved (Dedicated) at our "Pilot" support tier — the difference is predictability and unit price. A few clarifying bullets and I'll attach a worked example: 

- Quantization: 4-bit (q4) is broadly supported for the Llama-family variant we demoed; estimated token CPU/GPU time drops ~2.4x in our internal benchmarks, but payload/latency tradeoffs depend on sequence lengths and KV-hit rate.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduces token consumption for repeated context; if 40% of requests have shared prefixes you can see ~25–35% effective token reduction in generation.
- Credits vs. Reserved: credits are flexible, billed monthly; reserved gives ~18–28% unit discount at your target commit band and includes predictable burst capacity.

I attached an initial tier sheet and a short quant recommendations file. Jordan/Monica — can you upload a worked example for EW-4791 (50M tokens/month for 3 months) showing: raw token spend, expected savings from q4 + KV cache, and modeled credits vs reserved pricing?

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Sara Chen <sara.chen@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeWave - cost sketch and worked example (draft)

Hi all — attaching the draft Excel and the quick sketch below. See attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_EW-4791.xlsx (tab: pricing_sketch). High level: 

- Baseline (no quant, no cache): 50M tokens/month × $0.000035/token = $1,750/month (hosted rate example).
- With q4 quantization only: ~2.4x token-eff equivalence on GPU compute — modeled as 40% effective unit cost reduction => $1,050/month.
- With prefix/KV cache (conservative 30% hit on generative tokens): additional 25% reduction in billable tokens => combined modeled cost ~$787/month.
- Reserved commit offer: 3-month commitment of 150M tokens with a 20% discount vs hosted credit price gives total for term $3,360 (vs credits modeled ~$2,361) — reserved locks volume but gives lower per-unit.

Notes/assumptions are in the pricing_sketch tab. EdgeWave-specific tuning (longer sequences, multi-turn chat) will change the savings delta.

Sara — quick questions for accuracy: what % of your requests are repeated prefixes? And average completion length (tokens) per request? If you can send sample telemetry or a small histogram, we can refine the model.

—Jordan
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_EW-4791.xlsx (pricing_sketch)

From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@edgewave.ai>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeWave - cost sketch and worked example (draft)

Jordan — thanks, that spreadsheet is very helpful. Two clarifications: 

1) Our traffic is mixed — about 45% short prompts (<=32 tokens) for metadata enrichment, 40% multi-turn chat (avg 220 tokens completion), and 15% embeddings/batch scoring. The KV hit rate on multi-turn is currently ~28% (we think we can push to 45% with small prompt engineering).
2) Procurement asks if the reserved commit price is negotiable to match a blended price closer to the credits-model after factoring in expected cache+quant savings (i.e., can Redwood provide an elasticity concession if we commit higher volume after Q1?).

We'd like a two-part commercial structure: a) 3-month pilot on credits with an option to convert to a reserved 12-month commit at a pre-agreed band pricing, and b) an MOQ/commit ladder that gives us a mid-term reprice if we materially exceed the pilot baseline. Can Redwood draft that language?

—Sara

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@edgewave.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgewave.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeWave - term structure proposal and technical guardrails

Sara/Tom — looping in a proposed commercial structure and a short technical note on quantization caveats. Key points: 

- Commercial proposal (attached tier sheet v3):
  * Phase 1 (Pilot): 3 months, credits model. We provide a one-time 15% pilot credit uplift to accelerate evaluation.
  * Option to Convert: if EdgeWave elects to convert to a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days after pilot, we'll apply a conversion credit equal to 8% of committed spend as an onboarding credit and lock in the reserved unit price for the remainder of the 12-month term.
  * Upside Reprice: if monthly consumption exceeds pilot baseline by >30% for three consecutive months, both parties will reconvene to evaluate a volume-driven reprice (pre-agreed bands included in the tier sheet).

- Technical guardrails:
  * q4 quantization: recommended for customer workloads that tolerate slight accuracy drop; we suggest running parallel A/B evals on key prompt sets. Some generator decoders show small temperature sensitivity under q4 — Jordan can help tune defaults.
  * Cache priming: to hit higher KV rates we recommend a small prompt-engineering phase and a short-lived prefix canonicalization policy.

Attachments: EdgeWave_Optimize_Tier_Sheet_v3.pdf; quant_recs_edgewave.md

Tom — if procurement is comfortable, we can put the pilot SOW and DocuSign link on your desk this week. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the conversion language.

—Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the clear structure. Procurement is comfortable with the pilot uplift and the conversion credit mechanics. A couple of final asks before we sign: 

- Please add language that the conversion credit applies only if contractual conversion occurs within 30 days of pilot end; include a one-time prorated credit example in the SOW.
- Can Redwood commit to a technical onboarding window (SLA) for cache tuning? We propose a 4-week onboarding window with two dedicated SE sessions and a success checkpoint.

If you can update the SOW and DocuSign with those two items, we'll route internally and aim to sign by Friday.

—Tom
Head of Procurement, EdgeWave
